h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר י״ז Pesach — Maamar Yud Zayin

p: נוֹהֲגִין לִסְפּוֹר סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר אַחַר תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית,
It is customary to count Sefiras HaOmer after the Evening Prayer [on the second night of Pesach],
וְיֵשׁ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ לִסְפּוֹר אַחַר הַסֵּדֶר כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי:
while some authorities wrote to count after the Seder so that there should not be two contradictory actions:
שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר" כְּחוֹל הַמּוֹעֵד, וּמְבָרְכִין עַל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר.

reciting "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us regarding the counting of the Omer" as if it were Chol HaMoed (since in Eretz Yisrael the second night is Chol HaMoed), and then reciting blessings over eating matzah and maror [as on the first night of Yom Tov].
אַךְ כְּבָר דִּקְדְּקוּ מַה נַּפְקָא מִינָּהּ אִם קוֹדֶם הַסֵּדֶר אוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהוּא תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי
However, authorities have already asked what difference it makes whether it is before the Seder or afterward, since in either case it constitutes two contradictory acts
(וְעַיֵּין בִּתְשׁוּבוֹת חַיִּים שָׁאַל).
(see Teshuvos Chaim Sha'al).
וַאֲנוּ נוֹהֲגִין לְהַקְדִּים סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁהוּא מִן הַתּוֹרָה, דַּאֲנַן בְּקִיאִין בִּקְבִיעָא דְּיַרְחָא,
And our custom is to give precedence to Sefiras HaOmer because it is a Biblical obligation, as we are expert in the fixing of the calendar month,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קִידּוּשׁ וַאֲכִילַת מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר וְסִיפּוּר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל גָּלֻיּוֹת מִדְּרַבָּנָן.
whereas Kiddush, eating matzah and maror, and recounting the Exodus on the second day of Yom Tov in the Diaspora are Rabbinic.
אַךְ עַל כָּל פָּנִים קָשֶׁה שֶׁהוּא תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי.
Yet in any event, the difficulty remains that it involves two contradictory acts.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי, שֶׁיּוּכַל לִהְיוֹת שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים בְּנוֹשֵׂא אֶחָד וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת,
However, in truth, with Hashem, may He be blessed, there is no such thing as two contradictory matters, for two opposites can exist within a single subject and both be true
כְּעֵין שְׁאֵלַת יְדִיעָה וּבְחִירָה שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם עַל זֶה
like the question of Divine foreknowledge and human free will, regarding which the Rambam wrote
(הִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה פֶּרֶק ה' הֲלָכָה ה'):
(Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5):
כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר,
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts, etc.,"
וְהָרַאֲבַ"ד זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הִשִּׂיגוֹ דְּהָיָה לוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ בִּתְמִימוּת הַתְּמִימִים.
and the Ra'avad, of blessed memory, critiqued him that he should have left it to the simple faith of the pure.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ
And we have already explained
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּשֶׁב מַאֲמָר י"א)
(as elucidated in Parshas Vayeishev, Maamar 11)
שֶׁכְּדִבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ"ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּזֹהַר חָדָשׁ וּבְכִתְבֵי הָאֲרִיזַ"ל,
that what the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote is explicitly stated in Zohar Chadash and in the writings of the Arizal,
וְהַלָּשׁוֹן שָׁם שֶׁבְּמָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ יְדִיעָה שָׁם אֵין בְּחִירָה וְכוּלֵּי.
where the wording is that in the realm where Divine foreknowledge operates there is no free will, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ בְּעוֹלָם הָעֶלְיוֹן, ו' קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר נֶעְלָם מִמֶּנּוּ, שָׁם בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא יָדוּן עַל פִּי הַבְּחִירָה;
That is, in the upper world—the letter Vav, the Holy One, blessed is He, from Whom nothing is hidden—there He truly does not judge according to free will;
וְה' שְׁכִינְתָּא, שָׁם נִמְסַר הַבְּחִירָה, וְשָׁם לֹא יָדוּן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הַנְהָגָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי הַיְּדִיעָה.
whereas in the letter Hei, the Shechinah, there free will was entrusted, and there the Holy One, blessed is He, does not conduct His governance through foreknowledge.
וְאַף שֶׁהֵם תַּרְתֵּי דְּסָתְרֵי, אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי הֲפָכִים וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת,
Thus, even though they are two contradictory concepts, with Hashem, may He be blessed, two opposites exist and both are true,
וְעַל זֶה כָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: כִּי לֹא מַחְשְׁבוֹתַי מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר.
and concerning this the Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote that of this it is said, "For My thoughts are not your thoughts, etc."
וְכֵן כָּאן מְבָרְכִין עַל סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁהוּא מִן הַתּוֹרָה
And so too here: we recite a blessing over Sefiras HaOmer, which is from the Written Torah
קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי וְלֵית תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
"the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah, and Torah is nothing other than the Holy One, blessed is He"
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' ס'.)
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 60a)
וּמִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נִקְרָא הַפֶּסַח "שַׁבָּת", כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
and from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, Pesach is called "Shabbos," as it is said
(וַיִּקְרָא כ"ג, ט"ו):
(Vayikra 23:15):
מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת,
"From the morrow of the Shabbos"
קְדוּשָּׁה קְבִיעָא וְקַיְימָא מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
a fixed and enduring holiness from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, like the holiness of Shabbos,
וְלֹא נִקְרָא הֶחָג "שַׁבָּת" רַק אֵצֶל מִצְוַת סְפִירַת הָעוֹמֶר מֵהַאי טַעְמָא
and the festival is called "Shabbos" specifically in connection with the mitzvah of Sefiras HaOmer for this very reason
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ט"ו).
(as explained in Maamar 15).
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר כָּךְ יְכוֹלִים מִצַּד ה' תַּתָּאָה
Nevertheless, afterward we are able, from the side of the lower Hei
מַלְכוּת פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לַהּ
"Malchus is the mouth, we call it the Oral Torah"
לַעֲשׂוֹת גַּם בְּיוֹם זֶה קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
to establish on this second day as well the holiness of Shabbos,
וּמְסַפְּרִין בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם וּמְבָרְכִין עַל אֲכִילַת מַצָּה וּמָרוֹר כְּתַקָּנַת חֲכָמִים בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
so we recount the Exodus from Egypt and recite blessings over eating matzah and maror in accordance with the enactment of the Sages in the Oral Torah.

paragraphs.text: Rambam, Hilchos Teshuvah 5:5 — "Perhaps you will say: Does not the Holy One, blessed is He, know all that will be before it happens?… Just as a person cannot grasp the truth of the Creator… so a person cannot grasp the Creator's knowledge, as the prophet said, 'For My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor your ways My ways' (Yeshayahu 55:8). But we know without doubt that a person's deeds are in his own hands."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Beha'aloscha 12 — “In Atika there is no place at all for human action… only in the seven lower attributes, emanated toward the world of action, is there choice. On knowledge and choice the Rambam wrote that man cannot grasp the Creator’s knowledge, and the Ra'avad that it were better left to simple faith. In truth the Rambam’s words are also in the Zohar Chadash and the Arizal: in one place there is knowledge and there is no choice at all, namely in Atika… and only in the seven days of creation was choice given. Therefore at the third meal, when a Jew eats from the mouth of Atika, there is no place for Kiddush over wine, which is an arousal from below.” Connection: The same Rambam–Ra'avad dispute resolved by assigning foreknowledge and choice to different levels, applied to why the third Shabbos meal has no Kiddush.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Shaar HaEmunah, Divine Providence — “Israel believe in Hashem, that although to the eye there appear many modes of His governance that seem opposite to one another: sometimes Hashem shows His supernal governance, arousing the first kindness of creation, which was without any arousal from the creation… and sometimes He governs by the revealed conduct, ‘according to the pain is the reward’; and likewise it sometimes seems that man has choice and sometimes it appears that the power of choice has been taken from him, as in Avos, ‘All is foreseen and permission is granted’… yet all is from one root, and no mode of governance opposes another.” Connection: The same claim that foreknowledge and choice, though opposite to the intellect, are both true before God, stated as a principle of faith that Israel holds.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach) — "And we have learned that the Holy One, blessed is He, is called Torah; 'water' means only Torah, and Torah means only the Holy One, blessed is He."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Derush al HaTorah — “The Torah did not say to begin the counting on Yom Tov itself, for the beginning of the counting signifies toil, as is the meaning of bringing the Omer from barley, while the first day of Yom Tov signifies freedom. How could two opposites, freedom and toil, be at one time together? For opposites do not exist together. Therefore it had to write ‘from the morrow of the Shabbos,’ to say that specifically from the morrow of the day of cessation shall they count; for the cessation is theirs because they went out to freedom from slavery and labor, and they have a day of Shabbos and freedom on account of it.” Connection: Maharal sees the same opposition Rav Tzadok raises between the festival's Shabbos-like holiness and the counting, and gives it as the reason the Torah writes “Shabbos” in the Omer passage; Rav Tzadok goes on to hold that both opposites are true before Hashem.
